changes.before: Return the first element or a same-type fallback without converting the value.
changes.after: Reuse one function with different types while keeping its types connected.

before: A generic function uses a type parameter so one definition can work with several concrete types.

```swift
func repeatValue<T>(_ value: T) -> [T] {
    [value, value]
}
print(repeatValue("Hi"))
print(repeatValue(3))
```
T is String for the first call and Int for the second. Each returned array keeps its element type.
T links the types at several positions. It is not the same as allowing unrelated types at each position.
An array's first property is optional because the array might be empty. Use ?? with a fallback of the same type.
For the exercise, define firstOr<T>. Its array is [T], fallback is T, and returned result is T. Keep the first value when one exists; use the fallback only for an empty array.
after: A generic function works with more than one type. It uses a type parameter: a name that stands in for a type. In repeatValue<T>, T might stand for String in one call and Int in another.

```swift
func repeatValue<T>(_ value: T) -> [T] {
    [value, value]
}
print(repeatValue("Hi"))
print(repeatValue(3))
```
This prints ["Hi", "Hi"], then [3, 3]. Each call returns two copies of its input in an array. The text stays text, and the numbers stay numbers.
Within one call, each T means the same type. The input is T, and [T] means an array of that type. A generic function keeps that connection; it does not turn every value into text.
An array's first property may have no value when the array is empty. It is optional. The ?? operator chooses a fallback when that optional is nil.
Complete firstOr<T>. Take an array of T and a fallback of T, and return T. Return the first item when one exists. Return the fallback only when the array is empty.

before.question: firstOr<T> takes [T] and a fallback T. What does that repeated T express?
choices: The fallback and array element must use one consistent type for the call
before.explanation: The type parameter connects the input and output types. It preserves their relationship rather than converting values to a universal type.

after.question: What does T mean in both an array [T] and its fallback T?
choices: Both use the same type for this call
after.explanation: T connects the types. An array of numbers needs a number fallback, and an array of text needs a text fallback.
